class.name: NNConsideration
class.brief_description: Scores a behaviour from an input value and an optional activation curve.
class.description: Add [NNConsideration] nodes as children of [NNBehaviour], [NNBehaviourGroup], [NNConsiderationGroup], or scored [NNBTNodes] and [NNSTTickedNodes] nodes to contribute a score during evaluation. Each consideration node can contain an activation curve that can be defined in the node properties. The [member activation_input_value] property is used as the x-axis value to find the y-value on the activation curve. The y-value is then the resulting score for the consideration. If no curve has been set, the [member activation_input_value] will be used as the consideration score as-is. If a sensor or a sensor group is used as the input value for a consideration, the [member activation_input_value] for the consideration will be overwritten with the [member NNSensors.sensor_value] of the sensor node during evaluation. Otherwise the value of the consideration's [member activation_input_value] property will be used. In simple terms: sensors are optional, you can use considerations without them if you set the [member activation_input_value] directly in your code. A custom evaluation method can be defined for the [NNConsideration] node by extending the node with a script that implements [method on_evaluate], which returns the score. The score is recomputed on every evaluation, reading the [member NNSensors.sensor_value] of [member input_sensor] each time. Editing [member activation_curve]'s points at runtime therefore affects the next evaluation. In [method on_evaluate] you should return a value between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code]. You can sample the [member activation_curve] using [method sample_activation_curve]. You can also set [member NNConsiderations.has_vetoed] to [code]true[/code], which causes the parent behaviour or group to score [code]0.0[/code] and stop evaluating further considerations immediately. While [member NNConsiderations.has_vetoed] is [code]true[/code], evaluation returns [code]0.0[/code] immediately without reading [member input_sensor] or calling [method on_evaluate], and it is not reset automatically, so external code must set it back to [code]false[/code] to end the veto state.

method.name: on_evaluate
method.description: Called on every evaluation in place of sampling [member activation_curve] or using [member activation_input_value]. Return the score, typically between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code]. The current input is in [member activation_input_value], and [method sample_activation_curve] maps it through the curve. Setting [member NNConsiderations.has_vetoed] to [code]true[/code] vetoes the parent evaluation.

method.name: sample_activation_curve
method.description: Returns the y-value of the activation curve at [param input_value], or [code]0.0[/code] when no curve is set.

members.member: Optional [Curve] or [NNResponseCurve] that maps [member activation_input_value] to [member NNConsiderations.score]. When [code]null[/code], [member activation_input_value] is used directly as the score. Assigning any other resource type reports an error and keeps the previous curve.

The input value passed to [member activation_curve] (or used directly as the score when no curve is set). Typically in the [code]0..1[/code] range, though values outside that range are not clamped. When [member input_sensor] is assigned, evaluation overwrites this property with the sensor's [member NNSensors.sensor_value].

The sensor or sensor group whose [member NNSensors.sensor_value] is used as the [member activation_input_value]. When not set, [member activation_input_value] is used as assigned. If the node is freed, this property reads as [code]null[/code] and is treated as unset.
